To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

“Sliding mode stabilization of the Boost DC‐DC converter through ∑‐∆ modulation is possible and it can be done by using any average output feedback design, such as passivity based control, as long as it guarantees the uniform boundedness of the closed loop state and output signals”.
the ∑‐Δ modulation is an effective way to implement average dynamic output feedback controllers in switched systems.
the sliding mode control of the boost converter, based on a passivity based controller and implemented through a switched system with ON‐OFF inputs, is achieved through a ∑‐Delta‐modulator.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a sliding mode controller for the boost converter, which can be implemented in the discrete‐time domain, using a switched system.

the sliding mode stabilization of nonlinear systems by means of a switched implementation of average output feedback laws trough the use of a ∑‐∆‐modulator, which is a well known device in the analog signal encoding literature.
the sliding mode stabilization of DC‐to‐ DC converters, and in particular of the boost converter, through a switched implementation of average output feedback laws.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proposed sliding mode ∑‐Δ modulation control approach is able to provide an effective solution for the stabilization problem of a large class of nonlinear systems, which can be described by a general form of the boost converter, and for which only the output measurements are available.

the proposed ∑‐Δ modulation control approach is a powerful and flexible tool for the design of switched controllers with a number of desirable features such as: 1) a simple and straightforward synthesis of the switching logic; 2) a guaranteed stability and performance; 3) an effective implementation through a simple switched system.
the proposed approach is an effective way to implement continuous time sliding mode controllers on switched power converters.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed approach provides a systematic and flexible design methodology for the sliding mode stabilization of a class of nonlinear switched systems.

we are proposing a new control design framework for the stabilization of switched systems, which is a very important and challenging research field, where we are using a sliding mode control design, which has been widely studied in the last 30 years, and we are implementing it through a ∑‐∆‐modulator, which has been extensively used in communications, signal processing, analog‐digital conversion and so forth.

we have shown how to implement a continuous, average, output feedback sliding mode controller in a digital switched control framework, without the use of state measurements and with the possibility of transferring any average continuous controller design into the switched framework, thus making the design of switched controllers for nonlinear systems more accessible.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ∑‐Δ modulation control design is a viable alternative to the classical sliding mode control implementation, especially for the design of robust control laws in the context of nonlinear systems.

a switched system can be designed from an average controller by means of a simple, yet powerful, ∑‐Δ modulator, which allows to transfer the average controller's stability and tracking performance into a switched implementation.

the proposed approach is able to provide an efficient and effective way for the implementation of continuous, uniformly bounded, average controllers in the more restrictive discrete control framework of switched systems.
